sentences.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。

translations.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.
translations.idiomatic: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.

sentences.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。

translations.literal: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.

sentences.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。

translations.literal: You serve the inner palace in the empress's confidence; all say you foreknew the crown prince's deposition—should trouble erupt, disaster will reach you too.
translations.idiomatic: "You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too."

sentences.zh: 何不先謀之！」

translations.literal: Why not plot first!'
translations.idiomatic: Why not plot first!"

sentences.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。

translations.literal: Xiu reported to Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Lun accepted fully.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.

sentences.zh: 計既定，而秀說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，若得志之日，必肆其情性矣。

translations.literal: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, 'The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
translations.idiomatic: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, "The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.

sentences.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。

translations.literal: You have long served Empress Jia; street talk names you a Jia partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was branded Jia's man.

sentences.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。

translations.literal: Now even if you wish to build great merit for the crown prince, though he may swallow old rage for a time he cannot reward you—he will think you only reversed under popular pressure to escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.

sentences.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。

translations.literal: If any flaw appears you will still not escape execution.
translations.idiomatic: One slip and Lun's head would roll.

sentences.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」

translations.literal: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will.'
translations.idiomatic: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will."

sentences.zh: 倫然之。

translations.literal: Lun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Lun assented.

sentences.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。

translations.literal: Xiu therefore launched counter-espionage, saying men of the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.

sentences.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。

translations.literal: When the empress heard it she was terrified and ordered Court Physician-in-Chief Cheng Ju to compound croton and apricot-kernel pills.
translations.idiomatic: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.

sentences.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。

translations.literal: In the third month a forged edict sent Yellow Gate Sun Lü to Xuchang to murder the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。

translations.literal: Earlier the crown prince had feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food before him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.

sentences.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。

translations.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Lü reported this to Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince to a small compound and denied him food. Palace personnel still passed food to him over the walls.

sentences.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.

sentences.zh: 時年二十三。

translations.literal: He was twenty-three sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 將以庶人禮葬之，賈后表曰：「遹不幸喪亡，傷其迷悖，又早短折，悲痛之懷，不能自己。

translations.literal: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: 'Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: "Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.

sentences.zh: 妾私心冀其刻肌刻骨，更思孝道，規為稽顙，正其名號。

translations.literal: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.
translations.idiomatic: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.

sentences.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。

translations.literal: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.
translations.idiomatic: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.

sentences.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。

translations.literal: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.
translations.idiomatic: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.

sentences.zh: 妾誠暗淺不識禮義，不勝至情，冒昧陳聞。」

translations.literal: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize."

sentences.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。

translations.literal: An edict buried him with rites due Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The court buried him as Guangling prince.

sentences.zh: 孫惠

translations.literal: Section heading: Sun Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui.

sentences.zh: 初，趙王倫篡位，三王起義，制《己亥格》，其後論功雖小，亦皆依用。

translations.literal: At first, when Prince of Zhao Lun usurped the throne, the three princes raised the righteous army and established the 《Yihai Precedent》; afterward, in discussing merit, even small cases all relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun seized the throne, the three princes issued the 《Yihai Precedent》 to rank wartime merit, and afterward even small merit awards all continued to use that code.

sentences.zh: 頵意謂不宜以為常式，駁之曰：「聖王懸爵賞功，制罰糾違，斯道苟明，人赴水火。

translations.literal: Yun held that it should not be taken as a constant model and refuted it, saying, "The sage kings suspend ranks to reward merit and institute punishments to correct transgressions—if this way is clear, men will throw themselves into water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yun argued it must not become permanent law: 'Sage kings reward merit and punish crime—make that clear and men will walk through fire for you.

sentences.zh: 且名器之實，不可妄假，非才謂之致寇，寵厚戒在斯亡。

translations.literal: Moreover the substance of names and vessels must not be rashly lent; calling the unworthy talented is what brings bandits; the warning that thick favor lies in this perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Titles are not party favors; calling fools worthy invites rebellion; showering empty rank is how dynasties die.

sentences.zh: 昔孫秀口唱篡逆，手弄天機，惠皇失禦，九服無戴。

translations.literal: Formerly Sun Xiu mouthed usurpation and treason and with his hands played with Heaven's mechanism; Emperor Hui lost the reins, and within the nine domains there was none who wore the cap of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu preached treason and toyed with the edict; Emperor Hui lost control, and no one in the nine circuits wore the cap straight.

sentences.zh: 三王建議，席捲四海，合起義之眾，結天下之心，故設《己亥義格》以權濟難。

translations.literal: The three princes set up the plan; they rolled up the four seas; they combined the hosts of the righteous uprising and bound the mind of all under Heaven; therefore they established the 《Yihai Righteousness Precedent》 to weigh and relieve the hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The three princes swept the realm, welded the loyal armies, and issued the 《Yihai Righteousness Precedent》 as a temporary wartime ladder.

sentences.zh: 此自一切之法，非常倫之格也。

translations.literal: This was itself an expedient one-time law, not a standard for ordinary categories.
translations.idiomatic: That was an emergency rulebook, not a peacetime statute.

sentences.zh: 其起義以來，依格雜猥，遭人為侯，或加兵伍，或出皁僕，金紫佩士卒之身，符策委庸隸之門，使天官降辱，王爵黷賤，非所以正皇綱重名器之謂也。

translations.literal: From the uprising onward, according to the precedent it has been mixed and base: persons have been made marquis by pull, some added to the ranks of soldiers, some issued from black servants; gold and purple hang on troopers' persons; tallies and registers lie in menial slaves' gates—this is not what is called rectifying the imperial net and valuing names and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the code has handed marquisates to pull, put silks on privates, and stuffed tally books into lackeys' sleeves—that is not how you mend the net of state or honor a title.

sentences.zh: 請自今以後宜停之。」

translations.literal: I ask that from now on it be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Abolish it from this day forward.'

sentences.zh: 頵以孤寒，數有奏議，朝士多惡之，出除譙郡太守。

translations.literal: Because Yun was isolated and of cold background, he repeatedly had memorials and proposals; court gentlemen mostly hated him, and he was sent out as grand administrator of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yun had no faction and a cold pedigree; his blunt papers earned him enemies, and the court parked him as grand administrator of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 元康九年六月庚子，有桑生東宮西廂，日長尺餘；

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the sixth month of the ninth year of Yuankang, a mulberry tree grew in the western wing of the Eastern Palace, growing more than a chi a day;
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the sixth month of the ninth Yuankang year a mulberry sprouted in the western wing of the Eastern Palace and grew more than a chi a day;

sentences.zh: 甲辰，枯死。

translations.literal: on the jiachen day it withered and died.
translations.idiomatic: by the jiachen day it had withered away.

sentences.zh: 此與殷太戊同妖。

translations.literal: This was the same prodigy as under Emperor Taiwu of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: This matched the prodigy of Emperor Taiwu of Yin.

sentences.zh: 太子不能悟，故至廢戮也。

translations.literal: The crown prince could not understand, and therefore came to deposition and execution.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince failed to understand, and was deposed and killed.

sentences.zh: 班固稱「野木生朝而暴長，小人將暴居大臣之位，危亡國家，象朝將為墟也」。

translations.literal: Ban Gu said: "When wild trees grow in the court and shoot up violently, petty men will violently occupy the positions of great ministers, endangering and destroying the state—the court will become a ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu wrote, "When wild trees spring up in the court and grow violently, petty men will seize the posts of great ministers, endanger the state, and the court itself will become a ruin."

sentences.zh: 是後孫秀、張林尋用事，遂至大亂。

translations.literal: Afterward Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin soon held power, and great disorder followed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin soon seized power, and the realm fell into great chaos.

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十 范泰王淮之王韶之荀伯子

translations.literal: Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Huaizhi, Wang Shaozhi, Xun Bozi
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Zhunzhi, Wang Shaozhi, and Xun Bozi

sentences.zh: 義熙九年，上表曰：「臣聞咎繇亡後，臧文以為深歎；

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that after Gao Yao perished, Zang Wen deeply lamented;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yixi he submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that after Gao Yao perished, Zang Wen lamented deeply;

sentences.zh: 伯氏奪邑，管仲所以稱仁。

translations.literal: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong therefore praised its humanity.
translations.idiomatic: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong therefore praised the act as humane.

sentences.zh: 功高可百世不泯，濫賞無崇朝宜許。

translations.literal: Merit so high may be unextinguished for a hundred generations; reckless reward should not be permitted even for a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Merit so high may endure for a hundred generations; reckless reward should not be permitted even for a single morning.

sentences.zh: 故太傅鉅平侯祜，明德通賢，宗臣莫二，勳參佐命，功成平吳，而後嗣闕然，烝嘗莫寄。

translations.literal: Thus the late Grand Tutor, Marquis Juping Huo, was of bright virtue and penetrating worth, second to none among the imperial clans; his merit joined in assisting the Mandate, and when the work of pacifying Wu was accomplished, yet his later descendants were cut off and no one offered the seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Tutor, Marquis Juping Hu, combined bright virtue with penetrating worth and stood second to none among the eminent ministers; his merit joined in assisting the Mandate, and when the work of pacifying Wu was done, still his later line was cut off and no one offered the seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 漢以蕭何元功，故絕世輒紹。

translations.literal: Han, because of Xiao He's founding merit, whenever the line ended always continued the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Xiao He's founding merit, Han whenever the line ended always continued the succession.

sentences.zh: 愚謂鉅平之封，宜同酇國。

translations.literal: I humbly think the enfeoffment of Juping should be the same as the state of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe the enfeoffment of Juping should be treated like the state of Zan.

sentences.zh: 故太尉廣陵公陳淮，黨翼孫秀，禍加淮南，竊饗大國，因罪為利。

translations.literal: The late Grand Marshal, Duke of Guangling Chen Huai, aided and sheltered Sun Xiu; disaster fell on Huainan; he usurped enjoyment of a great state and turned crime into profit.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Marshal, Duke of Guangling Chen Huai, aided and sheltered Sun Xiu; when disaster struck Huainan he usurped enjoyment of a great state and turned crime into profit.

sentences.zh: 值西朝政刑失裁，中興復因而不奪。

translations.literal: It happened that the Western Court's government and punishments lost proper measure, and at the restoration they again followed precedent and did not revoke it.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Western Court lost proper measure in government and punishments, and at the restoration they again followed precedent without revoking the grant.

sentences.zh: 今王道惟新，豈可不大判臧否？

translations.literal: Now the royal way is newly renewed—how can one not greatly distinguish good from ill?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the royal way is newly renewed, how can one fail to judge good and ill on a grand scale?

sentences.zh: 謂廣陵之國，宜在削除。

translations.literal: I hold that the state of Guangling should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the state of Guangling ought to be abolished.

sentences.zh: 故太保衛瓘，本爵蕭陽縣公，既被橫禍，及進弟秩，始贈蘭陵，又轉江夏。

translations.literal: The late Grand Guardian Wei Guan originally held the enfeoffment of Duke of Xiaoyang County; having suffered violent death, when his younger brother's rank was advanced he was first posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling, then transferred to Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Guardian Wei Guan had originally held the enfeoffment of Duke of Xiaoyang County; after he suffered violent death, when his younger brother's rank was advanced he was first posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling and then transferred to Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 中朝公輔，多非理終，瓘功德不殊，亦無緣獨受偏賞，宜復本封，以正國章。」

translations.literal: Many grandees and assistants of the central court did not die natural deaths; Guan's merit and virtue were not exceptional, and there is no reason he alone should receive a partial reward—his original enfeoffment should be restored to rectify the state's regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Many grandees and assistants of the central court did not meet a natural end; Guan's merit and virtue were not exceptional, and there is no reason he alone should keep a partial reward—his original enfeoffment should be restored to set the state's regulations right."

sentences.zh: 詔付門下。

translations.literal: An edict referred it to the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the memorial to the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83

sentences.zh: 太子既廢，眾情憤怒。

translations.literal: Once the Heir Apparent was deposed, public sentiment was furious.
translations.idiomatic: Once the heir apparent was deposed, public anger boiled over.

sentences.zh: 有衛督司馬雅、常從督許超，皆嘗給事東宮，與殿中郎士猗等謀廢賈后，復太子。

translations.literal: The Colonel of the Guards Sima Ya and the Regular Colonel of the Followers Xu Chao, who had both once served the Eastern Palace, joined the Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others in plotting to depose Empress Jia and restore the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ya, Colonel of the Guards, and Xu Chao, Regular Colonel of the Followers, both former Eastern Palace attendants, joined Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others to plot deposing Empress Jia and restoring the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 以張華、裴頠安常保位，難與行權，右軍將軍趙王倫執兵柄，性貪冒，可假以濟事。

translations.literal: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei content to preserve their posts and hard to move to action, while the General of the Right Army the Prince of Zhao Sima Lun held military power and was greedy—he could be borrowed to accomplish the affair.
translations.idiomatic: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei too cautious to act, while Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, held the armies and was greedy—he could be used.

sentences.zh: 乃說孫秀曰：「中宮凶妒無道，與賈謐等共誣廢太子。

translations.literal: They thereupon said to Sun Xiu: "The central palace is fierce, jealous, and without the Way, and together with Jia Mi and others falsely deposed the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: They told Sun Xiu: "The empress is vicious and lawless. With Jia Mi she framed and deposed the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 今國無嫡嗣，社稷將危，大臣將起大事，而公名奉事中宮，與賈、郭親善，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一朝事起，禍必相及，何不先謀之乎！」

translations.literal: Now the state has no legitimate heir and the altars are in peril; the great ministers will raise a great affair, yet you by name attend the central palace and are intimate with the Jia and Guo—when the Heir Apparent was deposed all said you foreknew it. Once trouble rises disaster must reach you—why not plot first!"
translations.idiomatic: The realm lacks a legitimate heir and the altars are endangered. Great ministers will act, yet you serve the empress and are close to the Jia and Guo clans. When the heir apparent fell, men said you knew beforehand. When trouble erupts you will not escape—why not strike first?"

sentences.zh: 秀許諾，言於倫，倫納焉，遂告通事令史張林及省事張衡等，使為內應。

translations.literal: Xiu promised and spoke to Lun; Lun accepted, and reported to the clerks Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng among the communications staff to serve as inside agents.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu agreed and told Lun, who accepted and enlisted Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng as inside agents.

sentences.zh: 事將起，孫秀言於倫曰：「太子聰明剛猛，若還東宮，必不受制於人。

translations.literal: As the affair was about to begin, Sun Xiu said to Lun: "The Heir Apparent is intelligent, stern, and fierce; if restored to the Eastern Palace he will surely not be controlled by others.
translations.idiomatic: Before the coup Sun Xiu told Lun: "The heir apparent is clever and fierce. Restored to the Eastern Palace he will not submit to anyone.

sentences.zh: 明公素黨於賈后，道路皆知之，今雖建大功於太子，太子謂公特逼於百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳，雖含忍宿忿，必不能深德明公，若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。

translations.literal: Your Excellency has always been of the empress's party—the roads all know it. Though you now perform a great service for the Heir Apparent, he will say you acted only under the people's pressure and may turn to escape guilt; though he swallow old resentment he cannot deeply reward you, and if there be a flaw you still cannot escape execution.
translations.idiomatic: You have always sided with the empress—everyone knows it. Even if you now save him, he will think you acted only under public pressure and may turn on you to clear himself. Old grudges will not become deep gratitude; the slightest fault could still cost your life.

sentences.zh: 不若遷延緩期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，豈徒免禍而已，乃更可以得志！」

translations.literal: Better to delay and wait: the empress will surely harm the Heir Apparent; then depose the empress and avenge the Heir Apparent—not only escaping disaster but gaining your ambition!"
translations.idiomatic: Delay instead. The empress will kill him. Then depose her and avenge him—not merely escaping harm but winning your ambition!"

sentences.zh: 倫然之。

translations.literal: Lun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Lun agreed.

sentences.zh: 秀因使人行反間，言殿中人欲廢皇后，迎太子。

translations.literal: Xiu therefore sent men to spread counter-intelligence, saying those in the palace wished to depose the empress and welcome the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu spread disinformation that palace insiders meant to depose the empress and restore the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 賈后數遣宮婢微服於民間聽察，聞之甚懼。

translations.literal: Empress Jia often sent palace maids in plain dress among the people to listen; hearing this she was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The empress often sent maids in disguise to listen among the people and was terrified.

sentences.zh: 倫、秀因勸謐等早除太子，以絕眾望。

translations.literal: Lun and Xiu therefore urged Mi and the rest to eliminate the Heir Apparent early and cut off public hope.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and Xiu urged Mi and others to kill the heir apparent at once and end public hope.

sentences.zh: 癸未，賈后使太醫令程據和毒藥。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei Empress Jia had the Director of Imperial Physicians Cheng Ju compound poison.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the empress had Cheng Ju, Director of Imperial Physicians, prepare poison.

sentences.zh: 矯詔使黃門孫慮至許昌毒太子。

translations.literal: A forged edict sent the Yellow Gate Sun Lv to Xuchang to poison the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A forged edict sent Sun Lv of the Yellow Gate to Xuchang to poison the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子自廢黜，恐被毒，常自煮食於前；

translations.literal: Since his deposition the Heir Apparent feared poison and often cooked his own food beforehand;
translations.idiomatic: Since his deposition he feared poison and often cooked for himself;

sentences.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子於小坊中，絕其食，宮人猶竊於牆上過食與之。

translations.literal: Lv reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen then moved the Heir Apparent to a small compound and cut off his food, yet palace women still secretly passed food over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Lv told Liu Zhen, who moved him to a small compound and cut off food, though palace women still passed food over the wall.

sentences.zh: 慮逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，慮以藥杵椎殺之。

translations.literal: Lv forced the Heir Apparent to take the drug; he refused; Lv killed him with the drug pestle.
translations.idiomatic: Lv forced the drug on him; he refused; Lv beat him to death with the pestle.

sentences.zh: 有司請以庶人禮葬，賈后表請以廣陵王禮葬之。

translations.literal: The authorities requested burial with commoner rites; the empress memorialized for burial with the rites of a Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Officials requested commoner burial; the empress asked for princely rites as for the Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫、孫秀將討賈后，告右衛佽飛督閭和，和從之，期以癸巳丙夜一籌，以鼓聲為應。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu were about to attack Empress Jia; they told the Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants Lü He, who joined them, fixing the night of guisi on the second watch of the bing hour, with drumbeats as signal.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and Xiu prepared to move against the empress, won over Lü He, Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants, and set guisi night, second watch of the bing hour, drums as signal.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，秀使司馬雅告張華曰：「趙王欲與公共匡社稷，為天下除害，使雅以告。」

translations.literal: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join with you to steady the altars, remove harm for the realm—Ya reports this."
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join you to save the realm and remove this evil."

sentences.zh: 華拒之。

translations.literal: Hua refused.
translations.idiomatic: Hua refused.

sentences.zh: 雅怒曰：「刃將加頸，猶為是言邪！」

translations.literal: Ya angrily said: "The blade is at the neck—yet you speak thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Ya snapped: "The blade is at your neck and you still talk like that!"

sentences.zh: 不顧而出。

translations.literal: He left without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: He strode out without a backward glance.

sentences.zh: 及期，倫矯詔敕三部司馬曰：「中宮與賈謐等殺吾太子，今使車騎入廢中宮，汝等皆當從命，事畢，賜爵關中侯，不從者誅三族。」

translations.literal: When the hour came Lun forged an edict instructing the three departments' majors: "The central palace and Jia Mi and others killed our Heir Apparent; the Cavalry General will enter and depose the central palace—you must all obey. When done, enfeoffment as marquis within the passes; disobedience exterminates three clans."
translations.idiomatic: At the hour Lun forged an edict to the three departments: "The empress and Jia Mi killed the heir apparent. The Cavalry General enters to depose her. Obey and receive marquisates; disobey and face extermination."

sentences.zh: 眾皆從之。

translations.literal: All obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: All obeyed.

sentences.zh: 又矯詔開門，夜入，陳兵道南，遣翊軍校尉齊王冏將百人排冏而入，華林令駱休為內應，迎帝幸東堂，以詔召賈謐於殿前，將誅之。

translations.literal: He also forged an edict to open the gates, entered by night, arrayed troops along the southern way, sent the Colonel of the Supports the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong with a hundred men to force the gates and enter, the Commandant of the Hualin Park Luo Xiu as inside agent, brought the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and by edict summoned Jia Mi before the hall to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He forged orders to open the gates, entered at night, lined troops along the southern route, sent Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, with a hundred men to force entry, Luo Xiu of Hualin as inside agent, escorted the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and summoned Jia Mi to execution.

sentences.zh: 謐走入西鐘下，呼曰：「阿后救我！」

translations.literal: Mi ran beneath the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi fled to the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"

sentences.zh: 就斬之。

translations.literal: He was beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 賈后見齊王冏，驚曰：「卿何為來？」

translations.literal: When Empress Jia saw Sima Jiong she exclaimed: "Why have you come?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Sima Jiong the empress cried: "Why are you here?"

sentences.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」

translations.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to take the empress."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong said: "An edict commands your arrest."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也！」

translations.literal: The empress said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"
translations.idiomatic: She said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"

sentences.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢矣。」

translations.literal: She went up to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor from afar: "Your Majesty has a consort; when others deposed her, you too will be deposed."
translations.idiomatic: She climbed to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor: "You have a wife; when others depose her, you will be deposed yourself."

sentences.zh: 是時，梁王肜亦預其謀，后問冏曰：「起事者誰？」

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Liang Sima Rong also took part in the plot; the empress asked Jiong: "Who raised the affair?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang Sima Rong was also in the plot; she asked Jiong: "Who raised this?"

sentences.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」

translations.literal: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「系狗當繫頸，反系其尾，何得不然！」

translations.literal: The empress said: "When tying a dog one should tie the neck—instead they tied the tail; how could it not turn out thus!"
translations.idiomatic: She said: "Tie a dog by the neck, not the tail—was this not inevitable!"

sentences.zh: 遂廢后為庶人，幽之於建始殿，收趙粲、賈午等付暴室考竟。

translations.literal: She was thereupon deposed as commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were taken to the Severe Chamber for interrogation to the death.
translations.idiomatic: She was deposed as a commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were sent to the Severe Chamber for interrogation unto death.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書收捕賈氏親黨，召中書監、侍中、黃門侍郎、八座皆夜入殿。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Secretariat Supervisor, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered arrest of the Jia clan; the Secretariat Supervisor, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and Eight Seats were summoned at night.

sentences.zh: 尚書始疑詔有詐，郎師景露版奏請手詔，倫等斬之以徇。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing at first doubted the edict was false; Gentleman Shi Jing displayed the tablet and asked for a handwritten edict; Lun and the rest beheaded him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing doubted the edict; Gentleman Shi Jing asked for the emperor's own hand; Lun beheaded him as warning.

sentences.zh: 倫陰與秀謀篡位，欲先除朝望，且報宿怨，乃執張華、裴頠、解系、解結等於殿前。

translations.literal: Lun secretly plotted with Xiu to usurp the throne, wishing first to remove men of court esteem and also settle old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lun secretly plotted usurpation with Xiu, first removing leading ministers and settling old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others in the hall.

sentences.zh: 華謂張林曰：「卿欲害忠臣邪？」

translations.literal: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you wish to harm loyal ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you mean to kill loyal ministers?"

sentences.zh: 林稱詔詰之曰：「卿為宰相，太子之廢，不能死節，何也？」

translations.literal: Lin, claiming the edict, interrogated him: "You were chief minister; when the Heir Apparent was deposed you could not die for principle—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin, citing the edict, demanded: "As chief minister, when the heir apparent was deposed why did you not die for principle?"

sentences.zh: 華曰：「式乾之議，臣諫事具存，可覆按也。」

translations.literal: Hua said: "On the deliberation at Shiqian my remonstrance is fully recorded and may be reviewed."
translations.idiomatic: Hua said: "My remonstrance at the Shiqian deliberation is on record and may be reviewed."

sentences.zh: 林曰：「諫而不從，何不去位？」

translations.literal: Lin said: "If you remonstrated and were not obeyed, why not leave office?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin said: "If remonstrance failed, why not resign?"

sentences.zh: 華無以對。

translations.literal: Hua had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Hua had no answer.

sentences.zh: 遂皆斬之，仍夷三族。

translations.literal: They were all beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: All were beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 解結女適裴氏，明日當嫁而禍起，裴氏欲認活之，女曰：「家既若此，我何以活為！」

translations.literal: Xie Jie's daughter was betrothed to the Pei clan; the wedding was due the next day when disaster struck; the Pei wished to claim her alive; the girl said: "With my house thus, how can I live!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jie's daughter was to marry into the Pei clan next day when disaster struck; the Peis wished to save her; she said: "With my house destroyed, how can I live!"

sentences.zh: 亦坐死。

translations.literal: She too died for it.
translations.idiomatic: She died as well.

sentences.zh: 朝廷由是議革舊制，女不從死。

translations.literal: The court thereupon debated abolishing the old rule that daughters follow their kin to death.
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated abolishing the old rule that wives and daughters die with the clan.

sentences.zh: 甲午，倫坐端門，遣尚書和郁持節送賈庶人於金墉；

translations.literal: On the day jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent the Masters of Writing He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed Jia commoner to Jinyong;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed empress to Jinyong;

sentences.zh: 誅劉振、董猛、孫慮、程據等；

translations.literal: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;

sentences.zh: 司徒王戎及內外官坐張、裴親黨黜免者甚眾。

translations.literal: the Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and inner and outer officials dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and many inner and outer officials were dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei.

sentences.zh: 閻纘撫張華屍慟哭曰：「早語君遜位而不肯，今果不免，命也！」

translations.literal: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I told you early to yield your post and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I urged you to resign and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"

sentences.zh: 於是趙王倫稱詔赦天下，自為使持節、都督中外諸軍事、相國、侍中，一依宣、文輔魏故事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Zhao Lun proclaimed an edict amnestying the realm, made himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs, Chancellor, and Attendant, following the precedents of Xuan and Wen in assisting Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lun proclaimed amnesty, made himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief, Chancellor, and Attendant, following the precedents of the Sima regents of Wei.

sentences.zh: 置府兵萬人，以其世子散騎常侍荂領冗從僕射，子馥為前將軍，封濟陽王；

translations.literal: He stationed ten thousand troops at his headquarters; his heir, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment Fu, held redundant Followers as Vice-Director; his son Fu was Forward General and Prince of Jiyang;
translations.idiomatic: He stationed ten thousand household troops; his heir Fu, Regular Attendant, held redundant Follower posts; son Fu was Forward General, Prince of Jiyang;

sentences.zh: 虔為黃門朗，封汝陰王；

translations.literal: Qian was Yellow Gate Gentleman, Prince of Runan;
translations.idiomatic: Qian was Yellow Gate Gentleman, Prince of Runan;

sentences.zh: 詡為散騎侍郎，封霸城侯。

translations.literal: Xu was Gentleman of the Encampment, Marquis of Bacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was Gentleman of the Encampment, Marquis of Bacheng.

sentences.zh: 孫秀等皆封大郡，並據兵權，文武官封侯者數千人，百官總己以聽於倫。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu and the rest were all enfeoffed in great commanderies and held military power; civil and military officials enfeoffed as marquis numbered in the thousands; the hundred offices all reported to Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu and others received great fiefs and military power; thousands of officials were enfeoffed; all offices reported to Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫素庸愚，復受制於孫秀。

translations.literal: Lun was by nature mediocre and foolish and again controlled by Sun Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was mediocre and foolish and controlled by Sun Xiu.

sentences.zh: 秀為中書令，威權振朝廷，天下皆事秀而無求於倫。

translations.literal: Xiu was Secretariat Director; his authority shook the court; the realm served Xiu and sought nothing from Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu became Secretariat Director; power radiated from him; the realm served Xiu, not Lun.

sentences.zh: 中護軍淮南王允，性沉毅，宿衛將士皆畏服之。

translations.literal: The Central Protector of the Army, the Prince of Huainan Yun, was by nature deep and resolute; the garrison soldiers all feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, Prince of Huainan, Central Protector of the Army, was deep and resolute by nature, and the palace guards all feared him.

sentences.zh: 允知相國倫及孫秀有異志，陰養死士，謀討之；

translations.literal: Yun knew Chancellor Lun and Sun Xiu harbored rebellious intent and secretly nurtured men willing to die, plotting to attack them;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Lun and Xiu meant to rebel, he secretly gathered men willing to die and plotted against them;

sentences.zh: 倫、秀深憚之。

translations.literal: Lun and Xiu deeply dreaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and Xiu feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，轉允為太尉，外示優崇，實奪其兵權。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Yun was transferred to Grand Commandant—outwardly a mark of honor, in reality his military power was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, he was transferred to Grand Commandant, an outward honor that in fact stripped him of military command.

sentences.zh: 允稱疾不拜。

translations.literal: Yun pleaded illness and would not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 秀遣御史劉機逼允，收其官屬以下，劾以拒詔，大逆不敬。

translations.literal: Xiu sent the Censor Liu Ji to press Yun, seized his officials and subordinates, and impeached him for resisting an edict, great irreverence and impiety.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu sent Censor Liu Ji to coerce him, arrested his staff, and charged him with resisting an edict and great impiety.

sentences.zh: 允視詔，乃秀手書也，大怒，收御史，將斬之，御史走免，斬其令史二人。

translations.literal: Yun looked at the edict—it was in Xiu's own hand—and grew greatly angry, seized the censor, and was about to behead him; the censor fled and escaped, and two clerks were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yun saw the edict was in Xiu's own hand, flew into a rage, seized the censor and nearly executed him; the censor fled, and two clerks were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 厲色謂左右曰：「趙王欲破我家！」

translations.literal: With stern countenance he said to those at his side: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"
translations.idiomatic: He said grimly to his attendants: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"

sentences.zh: 遂帥國兵及帳下七百人直出，大呼曰：「趙王反，我將討之，從我者左袒。」

translations.literal: He thereupon led his state troops and seven hundred men of his personal guard straight out, shouting loudly: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled—I shall punish him; those who follow me, bare your left shoulder."
translations.idiomatic: He led his state troops and seven hundred household guards straight out, shouting: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled! I shall punish him. Follow me and bare your left shoulder."

sentences.zh: 於是歸之者甚眾。

translations.literal: At this very many came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Many rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 允將赴宮，尚書左丞王輿閉掖門，允不得入，遂圍相府。

translations.literal: Yun was about to go to the palace; the Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu closed the side gate, and Yun could not enter; he thereupon besieged the chancellor's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Yun marched on the palace, but Wang Yu, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, shut the side gate and blocked him; he then besieged the chancellor's residence.

sentences.zh: 允所將兵皆精銳，倫與戰，屢敗，死者千餘人。

translations.literal: The troops Yun led were all elite; Lun fought him and was repeatedly defeated, more than a thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's troops were elite. Lun fought him repeatedly and lost, with more than a thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 太子左率陳徽勒東宮兵，鼓噪於內以應允。

translations.literal: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, roused Eastern Palace troops and clamored within in support of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, stirred Eastern Palace troops to cheer within in support of Yun.

sentences.zh: 允結陳於承華門前，弓弩齊發，射倫，飛矢雨下。

translations.literal: Yun drew up his array before the Chenghua Gate; bows and crossbows fired together, shooting at Lun—arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Yun formed battle lines before the Chenghua Gate. Bows and crossbows volleyed at Lun until arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 主書司馬眭秘以身蔽倫，箭中其背而死。

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body; an arrow struck his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body and was killed by an arrow in the back.

sentences.zh: 倫官屬皆隱樹而立，每樹輒中數百箭，自辰至未，中書令陳淮，徽之兄也，欲應允，言於帝曰：「宜遣白虎幡以解鬥。」

translations.literal: Lun's staff all hid behind trees to stand; each tree received hundreds of arrows. From the hour chen to wei, the Secretariat Director Chen Huai—Hui's elder brother—wished to support Yun and said to the emperor: "The white tiger banner should be sent to halt the fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Lun's staff hid behind trees, each tree studded with hundreds of arrows. From chen to wei, Chen Huai, Secretariat Director and Hui's elder brother, wished to aid Yun and told the emperor: "Send the white tiger banner to stop the fighting."

sentences.zh: 乃使司馬督護伏胤將騎四百持幡從宮中出。

translations.literal: He then had the Major Fu Yin of the Protectorate lead four hundred horsemen bearing the banner out from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Major of the Protectorate Fu Yin was sent with four hundred horsemen bearing the banner from the palace.

sentences.zh: 侍中汝陰王虔在門下省，陰與胤誓曰：「富貴當與卿共之。」

translations.literal: The Attendant, the Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department; he secretly swore with Yin: "Wealth and honor shall be shared with you."
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant, Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department and secretly swore to Yin: "We shall share wealth and honor."

sentences.zh: 胤乃懷空板出，詐言有詔助淮南王。

translations.literal: Yin then carried a blank tablet out and falsely said there was an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Yin carried out a blank tablet and falsely claimed an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 允不之覺，開陣內之，下車受詔；

translations.literal: Yun did not perceive the deception and opened his ranks to admit him; Yun dismounted to receive the edict;
translations.idiomatic: Yun did not detect the fraud and opened his ranks. Yun dismounted to receive the edict;

sentences.zh: 胤因殺之，並殺允子秦王郁、漢王迪，坐允夷滅者數千人。

translations.literal: Yin thereupon killed him, and also killed Yun's sons, the Prince of Qin Yu and the Prince of Han Di; those implicated with Yun and exterminated numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then killed him, along with Yun's sons Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han. Several thousand connected with Yun were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 曲赦洛陽。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，孫秀嘗為小吏，事黃門郎潘岳，岳屢撻之。

translations.literal: Earlier Sun Xiu had once been a petty clerk serving the Yellow Gate Gentleman Pan Yue; Yue often flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiu had served as a petty clerk under Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Gentleman, who had often flogged him.

sentences.zh: 衛尉石崇之甥歐陽建素與相國倫有隙，崇有愛妾曰綠珠，孫秀便求之，崇不與。

translations.literal: Ouyang Jian, nephew of the Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, had long been at odds with Chancellor Lun; Chong had a beloved concubine named Green Pearl whom Sun Xiu asked for, but Chong would not give her.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Jian, nephew of Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, was estranged from Lun. Chong had a beloved concubine, Green Pearl, whom Xiu demanded and Chong refused.

sentences.zh: 及淮南王允敗，秀因稱石崇、潘岳、歐陽建奉允為亂，收之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Huainan Yun was defeated, Xiu thereupon claimed that Shi Chong, Pan Yue, and Ouyang Jian supported Yun in rebellion and arrested them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun fell, Xiu accused Chong, Yue, and Jian of supporting his rebellion and arrested them.

sentences.zh: 崇歎曰：「奴輩利吾財爾！」

translations.literal: Chong sighed: "These slaves covet my wealth!"
translations.idiomatic: Chong sighed: "These slaves want my wealth!"

sentences.zh: 收者曰：「知財為禍，何不早散之？」

translations.literal: The arresters said: "Knowing wealth brings disaster, why not have dispersed it early?"
translations.idiomatic: The arresters said: "If wealth brings disaster, why not have given it away?"

sentences.zh: 崇不能答。

translations.literal: Chong could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had no answer.

sentences.zh: 初，潘岳母常誚責岳曰：「汝當知足，而乾沒不已乎！」

translations.literal: Earlier Pan Yue's mother often reproached Yue, saying: "You ought to know sufficiency—why seize and scrape without end!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yue's mother had often scolded him: "Know when you have enough—why keep grasping for more?"

sentences.zh: 及敗，岳謝母曰：「負阿母。」

translations.literal: When disaster came Yue apologized to his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."
translations.idiomatic: When ruin came Yue told his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."

sentences.zh: 遂與崇，建皆族誅，籍沒崇家。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue, Chong, and Jian were all executed to the clan, and Chong's property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, Chong, and Jian were executed to the clan, and Chong's estate was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 相國倫收淮南王母弟吳王晏，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Lun arrested the Prince of Wu Yan, the Prince of Huainan's younger brother by the same mother, intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Lun arrested Yan, Prince of Wu, Yun's younger brother by the same mother, intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫傅祗爭之於朝堂，眾皆諫止倫，倫乃貶晏為賓徒縣王。

translations.literal: The Household Grandee Fu Zhi contended for him in the court hall; all remonstrated and stopped Lun, and Lun thereupon degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu county.
translations.idiomatic: Household Grandee Fu Zhi argued for him in court; all remonstrated, and Lun degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏以功遷游擊將軍，冏意不滿，有恨色。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi Jiong was transferred to General of the Reserves for his merit, but Jiong was dissatisfied and showed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was promoted to General of the Reserves for his merit but was dissatisfied and showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 孫秀覺之，且憚其在內，乃出為平東將軍，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu noticed it and, also fearing him within the capital, sent him out as General Who Pacifies the East, stationed at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu noticed and, fearing him in the capital, posted him out as General Who Pacifies the East at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 孫秀議加相國倫九錫，百官莫敢異議。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu proposed granting Chancellor Lun the Nine Bestowals; the hundred officials dared not dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu proposed granting Lun the Nine Bestowals; no official dared object.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書劉頌曰：「昔漢之錫魏，魏之錫晉，皆一時之用，非可通行。

translations.literal: Liu Song, Director of Personnel, said: "In the past Han bestowed them on Wei and Wei on Jin—all were expedients of the moment and cannot be made universal practice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song, Director of Personnel, said: "When Han bestowed them on Wei and Wei on Jin, those were expedients of the moment, not universal precedent.

sentences.zh: 周勃、霍光，其功至大，皆不聞有九錫之命也。」

translations.literal: Zhou Bo and Huo Guang achieved the greatest merit, yet one never hears of commands granting the Nine Bestowals."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bo and Huo Guang achieved the greatest merit, yet never received the Nine Bestowals."

sentences.zh: 張林積忿不已，以頌為張華之黨，將殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Lin, nursing his wrath, took Song for a partisan of Zhang Hua and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin, still furious, treated Song as Zhang Hua's partisan and meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 孫秀曰：「殺張、裴已傷時望，不可復殺頌。」

translations.literal: Sun Xiu said: "Killing Zhang and Pei has already harmed the age's esteem—we cannot kill Song again."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said: "Killing Zhang and Pei has already harmed public esteem. We cannot kill Song too."

sentences.zh: 林乃止。

translations.literal: Lin thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Lin desisted.

sentences.zh: 以頌為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Song was made Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Song was made Household Grandee.

sentences.zh: 遂下詔加倫九錫，復加其子荂撫軍將軍，虔中軍將軍，詡為侍中。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued granting Lun the Nine Bestowals; his son Fu was further made General of the Guards, Qian Central Commander of the Army, and Xu Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Lun the Nine Bestowals and further made Fu General of the Guards, Qian Central Commander, and Xu Attendant.

sentences.zh: 又加孫秀侍中、輔國將軍，相國司馬、右率如故。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu was further made Attendant and General Who Assists the State, retaining his posts as Chancellor's Major and Colonel of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was made Attendant and General Who Assists the State, retaining his posts as Chancellor's Major and Colonel of the Right.

sentences.zh: 張林等並居顯要。

translations.literal: Zhang Lin and the rest all held prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin and others all held prominent posts.

sentences.zh: 增相府兵為二萬人，與宿衛同，並所隱匿之兵，數逾三萬。

translations.literal: The chancellor's household troops were increased to twenty thousand, equal to the palace guard, and with hidden troops as well the number exceeded thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor household troops were raised to twenty thousand, equal to the palace guard; with hidden forces the total exceeded thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 倫及諸子皆頑鄙無識，秀狡黠貪淫，所與共事者，皆邪佞之士，惟競榮利，無深謀遠略，志趣乖異，互相憎嫉。

translations.literal: Lun and his sons were all obtuse and vulgar without understanding; Xiu was cunning, greedy, and licentious; those who worked with them were all depraved men who competed only for glory and profit, without deep plans or far sight, their aims divergent and mutually hateful.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and his sons were dull and vulgar; Xiu was cunning, greedy, and lewd. Their associates were corrupt men who sought only profit, without foresight, mutually hostile.

sentences.zh: 秀子會為射聲校尉，形貌短陋，如奴僕之下者，秀使尚帝女河東公主。

translations.literal: Xiu's son Hui was Colonel of the Archers; short and ugly in form, like one beneath a slave—yet Xiu had him marry the emperor's daughter, the Princess of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's son Hui, Colonel of the Archers, was short and ugly as a menial, yet Xiu married him to the Princess of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，甲子，立皇后羊氏，赦天下。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day jiazi, Lady Yang was established as empress and the realm was granted amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on jiazi, Lady Yang was made empress and the realm amnestied.

sentences.zh: 後，尚書郎泰山羊玄之之女也。

translations.literal: The empress was the daughter of Yang Xuanzhi, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: She was the daughter of Yang Xuanzhi, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 外祖平南將軍樂安孫旂，與孫秀善，故秀立之。

translations.literal: Her maternal grandfather was Sun Qi, General Who Pacifies the South of Le'an, on good terms with Sun Xiu, and therefore Xiu established her.
translations.idiomatic: Her maternal grandfather was Sun Qi, General Who Pacifies the South of Le'an, friendly with Xiu, which is why Xiu made her empress.

sentences.zh: 拜玄之光祿大夫、特進、散騎常侍，封興晉侯。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi was appointed Household Grandee, Special Courtier, and Gentleman of the Encampment, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingjin.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhi was made Household Grandee, Special Courtier, Gentleman of the Encampment, and Marquis of Xingjin.

sentences.zh: 廞自稱大都督，大將軍、益州牧，署置僚屬，改易守令。

translations.literal: Xin styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Governor of Yi Province, appointed staff, and changed the garrison commanders and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Xin styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Governor of Yi, appointed staff, and replaced local officials.

sentences.zh: 王官被召，無敢不往。

translations.literal: When court officials were summoned none dared not go.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials were summoned, none dared refuse.

sentences.zh: 李庠帥妹婿李含、天水任回、上官昌、扶風李攀、始平費他、氐苻成、隗伯等四千騎歸廞。

translations.literal: Li Xiang led his younger sister's husband Li Han, Ren Hui of Tianshui, Shangguan Chang, Li Pan of Fufeng, Fei Ta of Shiping, the Di Fu Cheng, Wei Bo, and others—four thousand horsemen in all—to join Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang led his younger sister's husband Li Han, Ren Hui of Tianshui, Shangguan Chang, Li Pan of Fufeng, Fei Ta of Shiping, the Di Fu Cheng, Wei Bo, and others—four thousand horsemen in all—to join Xin.

sentences.zh: 廞以庠為威寇將軍，封陽泉亭侯，委以心膂，使招合六郡壯勇至萬餘人，以斷北道。

translations.literal: Xin made Li Xiang General Who Subdues Bandits and Marquis of Yangquan Pavilion, entrusted him as close confidant, and had him gather braves of the six commanderies to more than ten thousand to cut the northern road.
translations.idiomatic: Xin made Li Xiang General Who Subdues Bandits and Marquis of Yangquan, trusted him deeply, and had him gather more than ten thousand braves of six commanderies to block the northern road.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 夏四月，歲星晝見。
value.en: Jupiter shone visible in broad daylight during the fourth month.
value.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the year star was seen in daytime.

value.zh: 冏將何勖、盧播擊張泓於陽翟，大破之，斬孫輔等。
value.en: He Xu and Lu Bo, under Prince Jiong, crushed Zhang Hong at Yangzhai and executed Sun Fu among others.
value.literal: Jiong’s generals He Xu and Lu Bo attacked Zhang Hong at Yangzhai, greatly defeated him, and beheaded Sun Fu and others.

value.zh: 辛酉，左衛將軍王輿與尚書、淮陵王漼勒兵入宮，禽倫黨孫秀、孫會、許超、士猗、駱休等，皆斬之。
value.en: On the xinyou day Wang Yu and Prince Cui of Huailing forced the palace gates, seized Lun’s confederates Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, and others, and put them all to the sword.
value.literal: On the xinyou day, General of the Left Guards Wang Yu, together with the minister, Prince Cui of Huailing, led troops into the palace, captured Lun’s faction Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, and others; all were beheaded.

value.zh: 逐倫歸第，即日乘輿反正。
value.en: Prince Lun was sent home under guard, and the emperor was restored to the throne that same day.
value.literal: They expelled Lun to return to his residence; that same day the imperial carriage returned to rectitude.

value.zh: 群臣頓首謝罪，帝曰：「非諸卿之過也。」
value.en: The ministers prostrated themselves in apology, but the emperor told them, “None of this was your doing.”
value.literal: The host of ministers knocked their heads in admitting guilt; the emperor said, “It is not the fault of you various ministers.”

value.zh: 癸亥，詔曰：「朕以不德，纂承皇統，遠不能光濟大業，靖綏四方；
value.en: On the guihai day an edict began: “Lacking virtue, I yet inherited the throne, and I have not been able to extend the great enterprise or bring peace to the four quarters of the realm;
value.literal: On the guihai day, an edict stated: “I, lacking virtue, have succeeded to the imperial line; afar I have been unable to brighten and aid the great enterprise and pacify and soothe the four directions;

value.zh: 近不能開明刑威，式遏姦宄，至使逆臣孫秀敢肆凶虐，窺間王室，遂奉趙王倫饕據天位。
value.en: Near at hand I failed to make law and majesty clear enough to stop treason, so the rebel Sun Xiu could brutalize the court, tear at the royal house, and help Prince Lun of Zhao seize the throne by force.
value.literal: Near I have been unable to open and clarify punishments and might and check villainy and treachery, so that the rebellious minister Sun Xiu dared unleash cruelty and violence, spy on and divide the royal house, and thereupon supporting Prince Lun of Zhao greedily seized the heavenly position.

value.zh: 鎮東大將軍、齊王冏，征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，並以明德茂親，忠規允著，首建大策，匡救國難。
value.en: General-in-chief who guards the east Prince Jiong of Qi, general-in-chief who conquers the north Prince Ying of Chengdu, and general-in-chief who conquers the west Prince Yong of Hejian are men of shining virtue and eminent kinship whose loyal counsel stood the test; they first devised the great plan that delivered the state from disaster.
value.literal: General-in-chief who guards the east, Prince Jiong of Qi; general-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian—all with bright virtue as flourishing kin, loyal plans truly manifest, first established the great strategy and rectified and saved the state’s crisis.

value.zh: 尚書漼共立大謀，左衛將軍王輿與群公卿士，協同謀略，親勒本營，斬秀及其二子。
value.en: Minister Cui framed the decisive plot; Wang Yu, general of the left guards, with the high ministers acting in concert, led their household troops into the palace and slew Sun Xiu together with his two sons.
value.literal: Minister Cui together established the great plan; General of the Left Guards Wang Yu, together with the host of dukes, ministers, and gentlemen, coordinated in stratagem, personally commanded the original camp, and beheaded Xiu and his two sons.

value.zh: 前趙王倫爲秀所誤，與其子等已詣金墉迎朕幽宮，旋軫閶闔。
value.en: The former Prince Lun of Zhao was deceived by Sun Xiu; he and his sons had already reached the Jinyong compound to bring me out of confinement and were turning their carriages toward the Changhe Gate.
value.literal: The former Prince Lun of Zhao was misled by Xiu; together with his sons and others he had already gone to Jinyong to welcome me from the hidden palace, turning the carriage at Changhe.

value.zh: 豈在予一人獨饗其慶，宗廟社稷實有賴焉。」
value.en: How could the blessing rest on me alone? The ancestral shrines and the altars of soil and grain have truly depended on them.”
value.literal: How could it be that I alone partake of the blessing? The ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain truly have relied on this.”

value.zh: 於是大赦，改元，孤寡賜穀五斛，大酺五日。
value.en: With the edict closed, the court ordered a general amnesty, a new reign title, five hu of grain for every widow, widower, and orphan, and five days of public feasting.
value.literal: Thereupon a general amnesty; the era name was changed; widowers, widows, and orphans were granted grain, five hu; great feasting for five days.

value.zh: 誅趙王倫、義陽王威、九門侯質等及倫之黨與。
value.en: Prince Lun, Prince Wei of Yiyang, Marquis Zhi of the Nine Gates, and the rest of Lun’s clique were put to death.
value.literal: Prince Lun of Zhao, Prince Wei of Yiyang, Marquis Zhi of Jiumen, and others, and Lun’s factional followers, were executed.

value.zh: 言之不從，是謂不乂
value.en: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.
value.literal: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.

value.zh: 元康九年六月庚子，有桑生東宮西廂，日長尺餘，甲辰枯死。
value.en: On gengzi in the sixth month of Yuankang 9, a mulberry shot up in the Eastern Palace’s west wing, grew more than a chi a day, and died on jiachen.
value.literal: Yuankang 9, sixth month, gengzi — a mulberry grew in the western wing of the Eastern Palace, lengthening more than a chi each day; on jiachen it withered and died.

value.zh: 此與殷太戊同妖，太子不能悟，故至廢戮也。
value.en: Like Shang precedent, the crown prince ignored the sign.
value.literal: This matches Yin emperor Taiwu's portent; the heir could not understand — hence deposition and slaughter.

value.zh: 班固稱「野木生朝而暴長，小人將暴居大臣之位，危國亡家之象，朝將為墟也。」
value.en: Ban Gu said: "Wild wood in court growing wildly means petty men will usurp ministers' seats — image of state ruin; the court will be waste."
value.literal: Ban Gu said: "Wild wood in court growing wildly means petty men will usurp ministers' seats — image of state ruin; the court will be waste."

value.zh: 是後孫秀、張林用事，遂至大亂。
value.en: Jia Nanfeng's minions fulfilled it.
value.literal: Thereafter Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin held power until great chaos.

value.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。
value.en: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.
value.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.

value.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。
value.en: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.
value.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.

value.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；
value.en: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;
value.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;

value.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。
value.en: Later ages styled her queen.
value.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.

value.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；
value.en: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;
value.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;

value.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。
value.en: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.
value.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.

value.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。
value.en: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.
value.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.

value.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。
value.en: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.
value.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.

value.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.

value.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」
value.en: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”
value.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”

value.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。
value.en: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.
value.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.

value.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。
value.en: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.
value.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.

value.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；
value.en: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”
value.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;

value.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。
value.en: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.
value.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”

value.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；
value.en: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;
value.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;

value.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。
value.en: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.
value.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.

value.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！
value.en: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!
value.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!

value.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。
value.en: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.
value.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.

value.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；
value.en: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;
value.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;

value.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。
value.en: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.
value.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.

value.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。
value.en: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—
value.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.

value.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；
value.en: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;
value.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;

value.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。
value.en: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.
value.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.

value.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。
value.en: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.
value.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.

value.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；
value.en: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;
value.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;

value.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。
value.en: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.
value.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.

value.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。
value.en: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.
value.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.

value.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。
value.en: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”
value.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.

value.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；
value.en: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;
value.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;

value.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。
value.en: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.
value.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.

value.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；
value.en: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;
value.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;

value.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
value.en: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.
value.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.

value.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
value.en: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.
value.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.

value.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
value.en: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;
value.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;

value.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。
value.en: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.
value.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.

value.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。
value.en: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.
value.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.

value.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。
value.en: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”
value.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.

value.zh: 及太子廢黜，趙王倫、孫秀等因眾怨謀欲廢后[8]。
value.en: Once Minhuai fell Sima Lun and Sun Xiu used hatred to target her [8].
value.literal: When crown prince deposed—Prince Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu exploiting resentment plotted depose consort [8].

value.zh: 后數遣宮婢微服於人間視聽，其謀頗泄。
value.en: She spied on rumors—some leaked.
value.literal: Consort repeatedly sent palace maids plain clothes among folk spy listen—plot leaked somewhat.

value.zh: 后甚懼，遂害太子，以絕眾望。
value.en: Terrified she murdered Minhuai.
value.literal: Consort greatly afraid—thereupon harmed crown prince—cutting off hopes.

value.zh: 趙王倫乃率兵入宮，使翊軍校尉齊王冏入殿廢后。
value.en: Sima Lun stormed in—sent Sima Jiong to drag her out.
value.literal: Prince Zhao Lun then led troops palace—ordered Colonel Qi Wang Jiong enter hall depose consort.

value.zh: 后與冏母有隙，故倫使之。
value.en: Jiong hated her mother—Lun used him.
value.literal: Consort with Jiong’s mother bore grudge—therefore Lun sent him.

value.zh: 后驚曰：「卿何為來！」
value.en: She cried, “Why you!”
value.literal: Consort alarmed said: “Why have you come!”

value.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」
value.en: Jiong said, "There is an edict to seize you."
value.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to seize you."

value.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也？」
value.en: She snapped, "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"
value.literal: Consort said: "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"

value.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢。」
value.en: Reaching the upper chamber she cried to the emperor, "Your Majesty has a wife, yet you let others depose her—you will be deposed yourself."
value.literal: Consort reaching upper chamber cried distant emperor: “Your Majesty has wife yet lets others depose her—you yourself will be deposed.”

value.zh: 又問冏曰：「起事者誰？」
value.en: She asked Jiong again, "Who raised this affair?"
value.literal: Again asked Jiong: “Who raised revolt?”

value.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」
value.en: “Liang and Zhao.”
value.literal: Jiong said: “Liang and Zhao.”

value.zh: 后曰：「繫狗當繫頸，今反繫其尾，何得不然！」
value.en: “Chain a dog by the throat—you seized the tail—no wonder!”
value.literal: Consort said: “Leash dog by throat—now leash tail—how can it not be so!”

value.zh: 至宮西，見謐尸，再舉聲而哭遽止。
value.en: Seeing Jia Mi’s corpse she wailed twice—then silence.
value.literal: Reaching palace west saw Mi corpse—raised voice twice weeping suddenly stopped.

value.zh: 倫乃矯詔遣尚書劉弘等持節齎金屑酒賜后死。
value.en: Sima Lun sent Liu Hong with golden liquor.
value.literal: Lun then forged edict dispatch Minister Liu Hong bearing tally deliver gold-filings wine grant consort death.

value.zh: 后在位十一年。
value.en: Eleven years queen.
value.literal: Consort held rank eleven years.

value.zh: 趙粲、賈午、韓壽、董猛等皆伏誅。
value.en: Her cabal died with her.
value.literal: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng executed.

value.zh: 惠羊皇后諱獻容，泰山南城人。
value.en: Empress Yang Xianrong came from Nancheng in Taishan.
value.literal: Empress Yang of Hui, taboo Xianrong, native of Nancheng in Taishan.

value.zh: 祖瑾，父玄之，並見外戚傳。
value.en: Her grandfather Yang Jin and father Yang Xuanzhi appear among outer kin.
value.literal: Grandfather Jin; father Xuanzhi—both treated in Outer Kin treatise.

value.zh: 賈后既廢，孫秀議立后。
value.en: After Jia Nanfeng fell Sun Xiu debated a new queen.
value.literal: After Empress Jia deposed—Sun Xiu debated establishing empress.

value.zh: 后外祖孫旂與秀合族，又諸子自結於秀，故以太安元年立為皇后[9]。
value.en: Sun Qi’s tie to Sun Xiu won her the throne in 302 [9].
value.literal: Consort maternal grandfather Sun Qi shared clan with Xiu—sons bonded with Xiu—therefore first Taian year established empress [9].

value.zh: 將入宮，衣中有火。
value.en: Fire sparked inside her robes on palace entry.
value.literal: About to enter palace—fire appeared within robes.

value.zh: 傅玄
value.en: Fu Xuan
value.literal: Fu Xuan.

value.zh: 倫篡，又為右光祿、開府，加侍中。
value.en: When Lun seized the throne, Fu Zhi became right grand master of splendid horses with independent establishment and added palace attendant.
value.literal: When Lun usurped, he again was right grand master of splendid horses, established office, added palace attendant.

value.zh: 惠帝還宮，祗以經受偽職請退，不許。
value.en: After Emperor Hui returned, Fu Zhi asked to resign for having served the usurper; the court refused.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui returned to the palace, Zhi because he had received illicit office asked to retire—not permitted.

value.zh: 初，倫之篡也，孫秀與義陽王威等十餘人預撰儀式禪文。
value.en: When Lun first usurped, Sun Xiu, Prince Yiyang Sima Wei, and a dozen others had drafted the abdication liturgy and text.
value.literal: At first when Lun usurped, Sun Xiu and Prince of Yiyang, Wei, and more than a dozen others pre-drafted the ceremonies and abdication texts.

value.zh: 及倫敗，齊王冏收侍中劉逵、常侍騶捷、杜育、黃門郎陸機、右丞周導、王尊等付廷尉。
value.en: When Lun fell, Prince Qi Sima Jiong arrested Liu Dai, Zou Jie, Du Yu, Lu Ji, Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others for the commandant of justice.
value.literal: When Lun fell, the prince of Qi, Jiong, seized palace attendant Liu Dai, regular attendants Zou Jie, Du Yu, yellow gate gentleman Lu Ji, right aide Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others and handed them to the commandant of justice.

value.zh: 以禪文出中書，復議處祗罪，會赦得原。
value.en: Because the abdication edict had issued from the secretariat, some wanted Fu Zhi punished, but a general amnesty spared him.
value.literal: Because the abdication text came from the secretariat, they again debated punishing Zhi's crime, but a general amnesty arrived and he was pardoned.

value.zh: 後以禪文草本非祗所撰，於是詔復光祿大夫。
value.en: Later it was shown the draft was not his hand, and an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.
value.literal: Later because the abdication draft in manuscript was not written by Zhi, thereupon an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.

value.zh: 子宣，尚弘農公主。
value.en: His son Fu Xuan married the princess of Hongnong.
value.literal: His son Xuan married the Princess of Hongnong.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。
value.en: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.
value.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.

value.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。
value.en: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
value.literal: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.

value.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。
value.en: "You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too."
value.literal: You serve the inner palace in the empress's confidence; all say you foreknew the crown prince's deposition—should trouble erupt, disaster will reach you too.

value.zh: 何不先謀之！」
value.en: Why not plot first!"
value.literal: Why not plot first!'

value.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。
value.en: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.
value.literal: Xiu reported to Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Lun accepted fully.

value.zh: 計既定，而秀說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，若得志之日，必肆其情性矣。
