value.en: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, "The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
value.literal: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, 'The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.

value.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。
value.en: Lun was branded Jia's man.
value.literal: You have long served Empress Jia; street talk names you a Jia partisan.

value.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。
value.en: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.
value.literal: Now even if you wish to build great merit for the crown prince, though he may swallow old rage for a time he cannot reward you—he will think you only reversed under popular pressure to escape blame.

value.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
value.en: One slip and Lun's head would roll.
value.literal: If any flaw appears you will still not escape execution.

value.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」
value.en: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will."
value.literal: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will.'

value.zh: 倫然之。
value.en: Lun assented.
value.literal: Lun agreed.

value.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。
value.en: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.
value.literal: Xiu therefore launched counter-espionage, saying men of the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome the crown prince.

value.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。
value.en: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.
value.literal: When the empress heard it she was terrified and ordered Court Physician-in-Chief Cheng Ju to compound croton and apricot-kernel pills.

value.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。
value.en: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.
value.literal: In the third month a forged edict sent Yellow Gate Sun Lü to Xuchang to murder the crown prince.

value.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。
value.en: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.
value.literal: Earlier the crown prince had feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food before him.

value.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。
value.en: Lü reported this to Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince to a small compound and denied him food. Palace personnel still passed food to him over the walls.
value.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.

value.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。
value.en: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.
value.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.

value.zh: 時年二十三。
value.en: He died at twenty-three.
value.literal: He was twenty-three sui.

value.zh: 將以庶人禮葬之，賈后表曰：「遹不幸喪亡，傷其迷悖，又早短折，悲痛之懷，不能自己。
value.en: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: "Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.
value.literal: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: 'Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.

value.zh: 妾私心冀其刻肌刻骨，更思孝道，規為稽顙，正其名號。
value.en: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.
value.literal: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.

value.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。
value.en: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.
value.literal: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.

value.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。
value.en: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.
value.literal: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.

value.zh: 妾誠暗淺不識禮義，不勝至情，冒昧陳聞。」
value.en: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize."
value.literal: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize.'

value.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。
value.en: The court buried him as Guangling prince.
value.literal: An edict buried him with rites due Prince of Guangling.

value.zh: 孫惠
value.en: Sun Hui.
value.literal: Section heading: Sun Hui.

value.zh: 初，趙王倫篡位，三王起義，制《己亥格》，其後論功雖小，亦皆依用。
value.en: When Sima Lun seized the throne, the three princes issued the 《Yihai Precedent》 to rank wartime merit, and afterward even small merit awards all continued to use that code.
value.literal: At first, when Prince of Zhao Lun usurped the throne, the three princes raised the righteous army and established the 《Yihai Precedent》; afterward, in discussing merit, even small cases all relied on it.

value.zh: 頵意謂不宜以為常式，駁之曰：「聖王懸爵賞功，制罰糾違，斯道苟明，人赴水火。
value.en: Chen Yun argued it must not become permanent law: 'Sage kings reward merit and punish crime—make that clear and men will walk through fire for you.
value.literal: Yun held that it should not be taken as a constant model and refuted it, saying, "The sage kings suspend ranks to reward merit and institute punishments to correct transgressions—if this way is clear, men will throw themselves into water and fire.

value.zh: 且名器之實，不可妄假，非才謂之致寇，寵厚戒在斯亡。
value.en: Titles are not party favors; calling fools worthy invites rebellion; showering empty rank is how dynasties die.
value.literal: Moreover the substance of names and vessels must not be rashly lent; calling the unworthy talented is what brings bandits; the warning that thick favor lies in this perishing.

value.zh: 昔孫秀口唱篡逆，手弄天機，惠皇失禦，九服無戴。
value.en: Sun Xiu preached treason and toyed with the edict; Emperor Hui lost control, and no one in the nine circuits wore the cap straight.
value.literal: Formerly Sun Xiu mouthed usurpation and treason and with his hands played with Heaven's mechanism; Emperor Hui lost the reins, and within the nine domains there was none who wore the cap of loyalty.

value.zh: 三王建議，席捲四海，合起義之眾，結天下之心，故設《己亥義格》以權濟難。
value.en: The three princes swept the realm, welded the loyal armies, and issued the 《Yihai Righteousness Precedent》 as a temporary wartime ladder.
value.literal: The three princes set up the plan; they rolled up the four seas; they combined the hosts of the righteous uprising and bound the mind of all under Heaven; therefore they established the 《Yihai Righteousness Precedent》 to weigh and relieve the hardship.

value.zh: 此自一切之法，非常倫之格也。
value.en: That was an emergency rulebook, not a peacetime statute.
value.literal: This was itself an expedient one-time law, not a standard for ordinary categories.

value.zh: 其起義以來，依格雜猥，遭人為侯，或加兵伍，或出皁僕，金紫佩士卒之身，符策委庸隸之門，使天官降辱，王爵黷賤，非所以正皇綱重名器之謂也。
value.en: Since then the code has handed marquisates to pull, put silks on privates, and stuffed tally books into lackeys' sleeves—that is not how you mend the net of state or honor a title.
value.literal: From the uprising onward, according to the precedent it has been mixed and base: persons have been made marquis by pull, some added to the ranks of soldiers, some issued from black servants; gold and purple hang on troopers' persons; tallies and registers lie in menial slaves' gates—this is not what is called rectifying the imperial net and valuing names and vessels.

value.zh: 請自今以後宜停之。」
value.en: Abolish it from this day forward.'
value.literal: I ask that from now on it be stopped."

value.zh: 頵以孤寒，數有奏議，朝士多惡之，出除譙郡太守。
value.en: Chen Yun had no faction and a cold pedigree; his blunt papers earned him enemies, and the court parked him as grand administrator of Qiao.
value.literal: Because Yun was isolated and of cold background, he repeatedly had memorials and proposals; court gentlemen mostly hated him, and he was sent out as grand administrator of Qiao commandery.

value.zh: 元康九年六月庚子，有桑生東宮西廂，日長尺餘；
value.en: On the gengzi day of the sixth month of the ninth Yuankang year a mulberry sprouted in the western wing of the Eastern Palace and grew more than a chi a day;
value.literal: On the gengzi day of the sixth month of the ninth year of Yuankang, a mulberry tree grew in the western wing of the Eastern Palace, growing more than a chi a day;

value.zh: 甲辰，枯死。
value.en: by the jiachen day it had withered away.
value.literal: on the jiachen day it withered and died.

value.zh: 此與殷太戊同妖。
value.en: This matched the prodigy of Emperor Taiwu of Yin.
value.literal: This was the same prodigy as under Emperor Taiwu of Yin.

value.zh: 太子不能悟，故至廢戮也。
value.en: The crown prince failed to understand, and was deposed and killed.
value.literal: The crown prince could not understand, and therefore came to deposition and execution.

value.zh: 班固稱「野木生朝而暴長，小人將暴居大臣之位，危亡國家，象朝將為墟也」。
value.en: Ban Gu wrote, "When wild trees spring up in the court and grow violently, petty men will seize the posts of great ministers, endanger the state, and the court itself will become a ruin."
value.literal: Ban Gu said: "When wild trees grow in the court and shoot up violently, petty men will violently occupy the positions of great ministers, endangering and destroying the state—the court will become a ruin."

value.zh: 是後孫秀、張林尋用事，遂至大亂。
value.en: Afterward Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin soon seized power, and the realm fell into great chaos.
value.literal: Afterward Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin soon held power, and great disorder followed.

value.zh: 列傳第二十 范泰王淮之王韶之荀伯子
value.en: Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Zhunzhi, Wang Shaozhi, and Xun Bozi
value.literal: Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Huaizhi, Wang Shaozhi, Xun Bozi

value.zh: 義熙九年，上表曰：「臣聞咎繇亡後，臧文以為深歎；
value.en: In the ninth year of Yixi he submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that after Gao Yao perished, Zang Wen lamented deeply;
value.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that after Gao Yao perished, Zang Wen deeply lamented;

value.zh: 伯氏奪邑，管仲所以稱仁。
value.en: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong therefore praised the act as humane.
value.literal: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong therefore praised its humanity.

value.zh: 功高可百世不泯，濫賞無崇朝宜許。
value.en: Merit so high may endure for a hundred generations; reckless reward should not be permitted even for a single morning.
value.literal: Merit so high may be unextinguished for a hundred generations; reckless reward should not be permitted even for a single morning.

value.zh: 故太傅鉅平侯祜，明德通賢，宗臣莫二，勳參佐命，功成平吳，而後嗣闕然，烝嘗莫寄。
value.en: The late Grand Tutor, Marquis Juping Hu, combined bright virtue with penetrating worth and stood second to none among the eminent ministers; his merit joined in assisting the Mandate, and when the work of pacifying Wu was done, still his later line was cut off and no one offered the seasonal sacrifices.
value.literal: Thus the late Grand Tutor, Marquis Juping Huo, was of bright virtue and penetrating worth, second to none among the imperial clans; his merit joined in assisting the Mandate, and when the work of pacifying Wu was accomplished, yet his later descendants were cut off and no one offered the seasonal sacrifices.

value.zh: 漢以蕭何元功，故絕世輒紹。
value.en: Because of Xiao He's founding merit, Han whenever the line ended always continued the succession.
value.literal: Han, because of Xiao He's founding merit, whenever the line ended always continued the succession.

value.zh: 愚謂鉅平之封，宜同酇國。
value.en: I humbly believe the enfeoffment of Juping should be treated like the state of Zan.
value.literal: I humbly think the enfeoffment of Juping should be the same as the state of Zan.

value.zh: 故太尉廣陵公陳淮，黨翼孫秀，禍加淮南，竊饗大國，因罪為利。
value.en: The late Grand Marshal, Duke of Guangling Chen Huai, aided and sheltered Sun Xiu; when disaster struck Huainan he usurped enjoyment of a great state and turned crime into profit.
value.literal: The late Grand Marshal, Duke of Guangling Chen Huai, aided and sheltered Sun Xiu; disaster fell on Huainan; he usurped enjoyment of a great state and turned crime into profit.

value.zh: 值西朝政刑失裁，中興復因而不奪。
value.en: It happened that the Western Court lost proper measure in government and punishments, and at the restoration they again followed precedent without revoking the grant.
value.literal: It happened that the Western Court's government and punishments lost proper measure, and at the restoration they again followed precedent and did not revoke it.

value.zh: 今王道惟新，豈可不大判臧否？
value.en: Now that the royal way is newly renewed, how can one fail to judge good and ill on a grand scale?
value.literal: Now the royal way is newly renewed—how can one not greatly distinguish good from ill?

value.zh: 謂廣陵之國，宜在削除。
value.en: I believe the state of Guangling ought to be abolished.
value.literal: I hold that the state of Guangling should be abolished.

value.zh: 故太保衛瓘，本爵蕭陽縣公，既被橫禍，及進弟秩，始贈蘭陵，又轉江夏。
value.en: The late Grand Guardian Wei Guan had originally held the enfeoffment of Duke of Xiaoyang County; after he suffered violent death, when his younger brother's rank was advanced he was first posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling and then transferred to Jiangxia.
value.literal: The late Grand Guardian Wei Guan originally held the enfeoffment of Duke of Xiaoyang County; having suffered violent death, when his younger brother's rank was advanced he was first posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling, then transferred to Jiangxia.

value.zh: 中朝公輔，多非理終，瓘功德不殊，亦無緣獨受偏賞，宜復本封，以正國章。」
value.en: Many grandees and assistants of the central court did not meet a natural end; Guan's merit and virtue were not exceptional, and there is no reason he alone should keep a partial reward—his original enfeoffment should be restored to set the state's regulations right."
value.literal: Many grandees and assistants of the central court did not die natural deaths; Guan's merit and virtue were not exceptional, and there is no reason he alone should receive a partial reward—his original enfeoffment should be restored to rectify the state's regulations."

value.zh: 詔付門下。
value.en: An edict referred the memorial to the Gate Department.
value.literal: An edict referred it to the Gate Department.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

value.zh: 太子既廢，眾情憤怒。
value.en: Once the heir apparent was deposed, public anger boiled over.
value.literal: Once the Heir Apparent was deposed, public sentiment was furious.

value.zh: 有衛督司馬雅、常從督許超，皆嘗給事東宮，與殿中郎士猗等謀廢賈后，復太子。
value.en: Sima Ya, Colonel of the Guards, and Xu Chao, Regular Colonel of the Followers, both former Eastern Palace attendants, joined Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others to plot deposing Empress Jia and restoring the heir apparent.
value.literal: The Colonel of the Guards Sima Ya and the Regular Colonel of the Followers Xu Chao, who had both once served the Eastern Palace, joined the Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others in plotting to depose Empress Jia and restore the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 以張華、裴頠安常保位，難與行權，右軍將軍趙王倫執兵柄，性貪冒，可假以濟事。
value.en: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei too cautious to act, while Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, held the armies and was greedy—he could be used.
value.literal: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei content to preserve their posts and hard to move to action, while the General of the Right Army the Prince of Zhao Sima Lun held military power and was greedy—he could be borrowed to accomplish the affair.

value.zh: 乃說孫秀曰：「中宮凶妒無道，與賈謐等共誣廢太子。
value.en: They told Sun Xiu: "The empress is vicious and lawless. With Jia Mi she framed and deposed the heir apparent.
value.literal: They thereupon said to Sun Xiu: "The central palace is fierce, jealous, and without the Way, and together with Jia Mi and others falsely deposed the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 今國無嫡嗣，社稷將危，大臣將起大事，而公名奉事中宮，與賈、郭親善，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一朝事起，禍必相及，何不先謀之乎！」
value.en: The realm lacks a legitimate heir and the altars are endangered. Great ministers will act, yet you serve the empress and are close to the Jia and Guo clans. When the heir apparent fell, men said you knew beforehand. When trouble erupts you will not escape—why not strike first?"
value.literal: Now the state has no legitimate heir and the altars are in peril; the great ministers will raise a great affair, yet you by name attend the central palace and are intimate with the Jia and Guo—when the Heir Apparent was deposed all said you foreknew it. Once trouble rises disaster must reach you—why not plot first!"

value.zh: 秀許諾，言於倫，倫納焉，遂告通事令史張林及省事張衡等，使為內應。
value.en: Xiu agreed and told Lun, who accepted and enlisted Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng as inside agents.
value.literal: Xiu promised and spoke to Lun; Lun accepted, and reported to the clerks Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng among the communications staff to serve as inside agents.

value.zh: 事將起，孫秀言於倫曰：「太子聰明剛猛，若還東宮，必不受制於人。
value.en: Before the coup Sun Xiu told Lun: "The heir apparent is clever and fierce. Restored to the Eastern Palace he will not submit to anyone.
value.literal: As the affair was about to begin, Sun Xiu said to Lun: "The Heir Apparent is intelligent, stern, and fierce; if restored to the Eastern Palace he will surely not be controlled by others.

value.zh: 明公素黨於賈后，道路皆知之，今雖建大功於太子，太子謂公特逼於百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳，雖含忍宿忿，必不能深德明公，若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
value.en: You have always sided with the empress—everyone knows it. Even if you now save him, he will think you acted only under public pressure and may turn on you to clear himself. Old grudges will not become deep gratitude; the slightest fault could still cost your life.
value.literal: Your Excellency has always been of the empress's party—the roads all know it. Though you now perform a great service for the Heir Apparent, he will say you acted only under the people's pressure and may turn to escape guilt; though he swallow old resentment he cannot deeply reward you, and if there be a flaw you still cannot escape execution.

value.zh: 不若遷延緩期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，豈徒免禍而已，乃更可以得志！」
value.en: Delay instead. The empress will kill him. Then depose her and avenge him—not merely escaping harm but winning your ambition!"
value.literal: Better to delay and wait: the empress will surely harm the Heir Apparent; then depose the empress and avenge the Heir Apparent—not only escaping disaster but gaining your ambition!"

value.zh: 倫然之。
value.en: Lun agreed.
value.literal: Lun agreed.

value.zh: 秀因使人行反間，言殿中人欲廢皇后，迎太子。
value.en: Xiu spread disinformation that palace insiders meant to depose the empress and restore the heir apparent.
value.literal: Xiu therefore sent men to spread counter-intelligence, saying those in the palace wished to depose the empress and welcome the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 賈后數遣宮婢微服於民間聽察，聞之甚懼。
value.en: The empress often sent maids in disguise to listen among the people and was terrified.
value.literal: Empress Jia often sent palace maids in plain dress among the people to listen; hearing this she was greatly afraid.

value.zh: 倫、秀因勸謐等早除太子，以絕眾望。
value.en: Lun and Xiu urged Mi and others to kill the heir apparent at once and end public hope.
value.literal: Lun and Xiu therefore urged Mi and the rest to eliminate the Heir Apparent early and cut off public hope.

value.zh: 癸未，賈后使太醫令程據和毒藥。
value.en: On guiwei the empress had Cheng Ju, Director of Imperial Physicians, prepare poison.
value.literal: On the day guiwei Empress Jia had the Director of Imperial Physicians Cheng Ju compound poison.

value.zh: 矯詔使黃門孫慮至許昌毒太子。
value.en: A forged edict sent Sun Lv of the Yellow Gate to Xuchang to poison the heir apparent.
value.literal: A forged edict sent the Yellow Gate Sun Lv to Xuchang to poison the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 太子自廢黜，恐被毒，常自煮食於前；
value.en: Since his deposition he feared poison and often cooked for himself;
value.literal: Since his deposition the Heir Apparent feared poison and often cooked his own food beforehand;

value.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子於小坊中，絕其食，宮人猶竊於牆上過食與之。
value.en: Lv told Liu Zhen, who moved him to a small compound and cut off food, though palace women still passed food over the wall.
value.literal: Lv reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen then moved the Heir Apparent to a small compound and cut off his food, yet palace women still secretly passed food over the wall.

value.zh: 慮逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，慮以藥杵椎殺之。
value.en: Lv forced the drug on him; he refused; Lv beat him to death with the pestle.
value.literal: Lv forced the Heir Apparent to take the drug; he refused; Lv killed him with the drug pestle.

value.zh: 有司請以庶人禮葬，賈后表請以廣陵王禮葬之。
value.en: Officials requested commoner burial; the empress asked for princely rites as for the Prince of Guangling.
value.literal: The authorities requested burial with commoner rites; the empress memorialized for burial with the rites of a Prince of Guangling.

value.zh: 趙王倫、孫秀將討賈后，告右衛佽飛督閭和，和從之，期以癸巳丙夜一籌，以鼓聲為應。
value.en: Lun and Xiu prepared to move against the empress, won over Lü He, Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants, and set guisi night, second watch of the bing hour, drums as signal.
value.literal: The Prince of Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu were about to attack Empress Jia; they told the Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants Lü He, who joined them, fixing the night of guisi on the second watch of the bing hour, with drumbeats as signal.

value.zh: 癸巳，秀使司馬雅告張華曰：「趙王欲與公共匡社稷，為天下除害，使雅以告。」
value.en: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join you to save the realm and remove this evil."
value.literal: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join with you to steady the altars, remove harm for the realm—Ya reports this."

value.zh: 華拒之。
value.en: Hua refused.
value.literal: Hua refused.

value.zh: 雅怒曰：「刃將加頸，猶為是言邪！」
value.en: Ya snapped: "The blade is at your neck and you still talk like that!"
value.literal: Ya angrily said: "The blade is at the neck—yet you speak thus!"

value.zh: 不顧而出。
value.en: He strode out without a backward glance.
value.literal: He left without looking back.

value.zh: 及期，倫矯詔敕三部司馬曰：「中宮與賈謐等殺吾太子，今使車騎入廢中宮，汝等皆當從命，事畢，賜爵關中侯，不從者誅三族。」
value.en: At the hour Lun forged an edict to the three departments: "The empress and Jia Mi killed the heir apparent. The Cavalry General enters to depose her. Obey and receive marquisates; disobey and face extermination."
value.literal: When the hour came Lun forged an edict instructing the three departments' majors: "The central palace and Jia Mi and others killed our Heir Apparent; the Cavalry General will enter and depose the central palace—you must all obey. When done, enfeoffment as marquis within the passes; disobedience exterminates three clans."

value.zh: 眾皆從之。
value.en: All obeyed.
value.literal: All obeyed.

value.zh: 又矯詔開門，夜入，陳兵道南，遣翊軍校尉齊王冏將百人排冏而入，華林令駱休為內應，迎帝幸東堂，以詔召賈謐於殿前，將誅之。
value.en: He forged orders to open the gates, entered at night, lined troops along the southern route, sent Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, with a hundred men to force entry, Luo Xiu of Hualin as inside agent, escorted the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and summoned Jia Mi to execution.
value.literal: He also forged an edict to open the gates, entered by night, arrayed troops along the southern way, sent the Colonel of the Supports the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong with a hundred men to force the gates and enter, the Commandant of the Hualin Park Luo Xiu as inside agent, brought the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and by edict summoned Jia Mi before the hall to be executed.

value.zh: 謐走入西鐘下，呼曰：「阿后救我！」
value.en: Mi fled to the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"
value.literal: Mi ran beneath the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"

value.zh: 就斬之。
value.en: He was beheaded at once.
value.literal: He was beheaded on the spot.

value.zh: 賈后見齊王冏，驚曰：「卿何為來？」
value.en: Seeing Sima Jiong the empress cried: "Why are you here?"
value.literal: When Empress Jia saw Sima Jiong she exclaimed: "Why have you come?"

value.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」
value.en: Jiong said: "An edict commands your arrest."
value.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to take the empress."

value.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也！」
value.en: She said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"
value.literal: The empress said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"

value.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢矣。」
value.en: She climbed to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor: "You have a wife; when others depose her, you will be deposed yourself."
value.literal: She went up to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor from afar: "Your Majesty has a consort; when others deposed her, you too will be deposed."

value.zh: 是時，梁王肜亦預其謀，后問冏曰：「起事者誰？」
value.en: The Prince of Liang Sima Rong was also in the plot; she asked Jiong: "Who raised this?"
value.literal: At that time the Prince of Liang Sima Rong also took part in the plot; the empress asked Jiong: "Who raised the affair?"

value.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」
value.en: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."
value.literal: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."

value.zh: 后曰：「系狗當繫頸，反系其尾，何得不然！」
value.en: She said: "Tie a dog by the neck, not the tail—was this not inevitable!"
value.literal: The empress said: "When tying a dog one should tie the neck—instead they tied the tail; how could it not turn out thus!"

value.zh: 遂廢后為庶人，幽之於建始殿，收趙粲、賈午等付暴室考竟。
value.en: She was deposed as a commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were sent to the Severe Chamber for interrogation unto death.
value.literal: She was thereupon deposed as commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were taken to the Severe Chamber for interrogation to the death.

value.zh: 詔尚書收捕賈氏親黨，召中書監、侍中、黃門侍郎、八座皆夜入殿。
value.en: An edict ordered arrest of the Jia clan; the Secretariat Supervisor, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and Eight Seats were summoned at night.
value.literal: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Secretariat Supervisor, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.

value.zh: 尚書始疑詔有詐，郎師景露版奏請手詔，倫等斬之以徇。
value.en: The Masters of Writing doubted the edict; Gentleman Shi Jing asked for the emperor's own hand; Lun beheaded him as warning.
value.literal: The Masters of Writing at first doubted the edict was false; Gentleman Shi Jing displayed the tablet and asked for a handwritten edict; Lun and the rest beheaded him as a warning.

value.zh: 倫陰與秀謀篡位，欲先除朝望，且報宿怨，乃執張華、裴頠、解系、解結等於殿前。
value.en: Lun secretly plotted usurpation with Xiu, first removing leading ministers and settling old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others in the hall.
value.literal: Lun secretly plotted with Xiu to usurp the throne, wishing first to remove men of court esteem and also settle old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others before the hall.

value.zh: 華謂張林曰：「卿欲害忠臣邪？」
value.en: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you mean to kill loyal ministers?"
value.literal: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you wish to harm loyal ministers?"

value.zh: 林稱詔詰之曰：「卿為宰相，太子之廢，不能死節，何也？」
value.en: Lin, citing the edict, demanded: "As chief minister, when the heir apparent was deposed why did you not die for principle?"
value.literal: Lin, claiming the edict, interrogated him: "You were chief minister; when the Heir Apparent was deposed you could not die for principle—why?"

value.zh: 華曰：「式乾之議，臣諫事具存，可覆按也。」
value.en: Hua said: "My remonstrance at the Shiqian deliberation is on record and may be reviewed."
value.literal: Hua said: "On the deliberation at Shiqian my remonstrance is fully recorded and may be reviewed."

value.zh: 林曰：「諫而不從，何不去位？」
value.en: Lin said: "If remonstrance failed, why not resign?"
value.literal: Lin said: "If you remonstrated and were not obeyed, why not leave office?"

value.zh: 華無以對。
value.en: Hua had no answer.
value.literal: Hua had no reply.

value.zh: 遂皆斬之，仍夷三族。
value.en: All were beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.
value.literal: They were all beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.

value.zh: 解結女適裴氏，明日當嫁而禍起，裴氏欲認活之，女曰：「家既若此，我何以活為！」
value.en: Xie Jie's daughter was to marry into the Pei clan next day when disaster struck; the Peis wished to save her; she said: "With my house destroyed, how can I live!"
value.literal: Xie Jie's daughter was betrothed to the Pei clan; the wedding was due the next day when disaster struck; the Pei wished to claim her alive; the girl said: "With my house thus, how can I live!"

value.zh: 亦坐死。
value.en: She died as well.
value.literal: She too died for it.

value.zh: 朝廷由是議革舊制，女不從死。
value.en: The court then debated abolishing the old rule that wives and daughters die with the clan.
value.literal: The court thereupon debated abolishing the old rule that daughters follow their kin to death.

value.zh: 甲午，倫坐端門，遣尚書和郁持節送賈庶人於金墉；
value.en: On jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed empress to Jinyong;
value.literal: On the day jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent the Masters of Writing He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed Jia commoner to Jinyong;

value.zh: 誅劉振、董猛、孫慮、程據等；
value.en: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;
value.literal: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;

value.zh: 司徒王戎及內外官坐張、裴親黨黜免者甚眾。
value.en: Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and many inner and outer officials were dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei.
value.literal: the Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and inner and outer officials dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei were very numerous.

value.zh: 閻纘撫張華屍慟哭曰：「早語君遜位而不肯，今果不免，命也！」
value.en: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I urged you to resign and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"
value.literal: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I told you early to yield your post and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"

value.zh: 於是趙王倫稱詔赦天下，自為使持節、都督中外諸軍事、相國、侍中，一依宣、文輔魏故事。
value.en: Lun proclaimed amnesty, made himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief, Chancellor, and Attendant, following the precedents of the Sima regents of Wei.
value.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Zhao Lun proclaimed an edict amnestying the realm, made himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs, Chancellor, and Attendant, following the precedents of Xuan and Wen in assisting Wei.

value.zh: 置府兵萬人，以其世子散騎常侍荂領冗從僕射，子馥為前將軍，封濟陽王；
value.en: He stationed ten thousand household troops; his heir Fu, Regular Attendant, held redundant Follower posts; son Fu was Forward General, Prince of Jiyang;
value.literal: He stationed ten thousand troops at his headquarters; his heir, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment Fu, held redundant Followers as Vice-Director; his son Fu was Forward General and Prince of Jiyang;
